sam: Quick alert — saw p95 spike for short chats when KV hit drops under ~60%. Looks like batcher is waiting for prefetch hits and assembling bigger batches that mismatch kernel profile.
anya: numbers?
sam: baseline p95_total=110ms current=230ms. assemble p95 went +90ms. kernel exec unchanged. Assembly + wait for kv_prefetch is culprit.
leo: What's current snap/holdback config and kv prefetch_tokens?
sam: holdback_ms=18, snap_timer_ms=3, prefetch_tokens=10, token_budget_target=64
marco: Prefetch_tokens 10 seems high — longer tail to wait. Also kernel selection flips when batch size >12; mixed-size batches force slower kernel.
rachel: So KV misses cause more requeues and then we get a few big mixed batches that pick CPU kernel. We should avoid mixing tiny requests with long ones.
anya: Proposal: add tiny-fast-path: requests <=6 tokens bypass holdback and are admitted immediately with a fast-path kernel hint. Keep a micro-snap timer (5ms) that only coalesces same-size buckets.
leo: Add tracepoints: batch_assembled_size, batch_kernel_choice, kv_wait_duration, requeue_count. We'll need cohort tagging for canary.
sam: I'll run a canary: cohort A (holdback_ms=5, prefetch_tokens=2, tiny-bypass<=6), cohort B (holdback_ms=18, prefetch_tokens=10 with short-bypass). 2h run.
marco: Also implement an adaptive soft-429 policy: when assemble_p95 > 200ms and queue_depth > 90th percentile, probabilistically soft-429 requests >100 tokens. Probability ramps based on assemble_p95.
rachel: Add metric kv_miss_requeues and kernel_mismatch_rate (fraction of batches with mixed-length that choose slow kernel).
perf-ci-bot: perf snapshot created: run_id=perf-1748899999-01, workload=chat_mixed_kv_swing, baseline_ts=1748800000, current_ts=1748899999
anya: Good. Also consider token_budget_target tweak: make it a sliding target based on measured kv_hit_rate to avoid starving small batches when KV hit rate drops.
sam: Action items:
- sam: deploy tracepoints, start canary, post run id + early graphs
- leo: dashboard: assemble_p95 by kv_hit/miss, cohort, size-bucket, kernel_choice
- marco: implement adaptive soft-429 and kernel hinting for tiny path
- anya: patch tiny-bypass <=6 + sliding token_budget heuristic
- rachel: add kv_miss_requeues & kernel_mismatch_rate metrics
Anyone opposed to running canary now? :eyes:
leo: go for it; I'll be on watch.
marco: lgtm
rachel: fine
sam: starting canary in ~10m, will post perf link early
